effectiveGovernance.historicalSourceStatus: Original missing-source rows below are preserved, not reconstructed.

notice: Source inventory and dependency order only. No implementation, live activation, approval or independent enforcement is asserted. Depth is a lower bound; external prerequisites and policy approvals are additional gates.

sourceCells: assertGRO() runs before every LLM call and on all LLM output. Non-compressible
applyScoreSync() is the only writer to users.arkScore; direct database writes are prohibited
Every prompt performs exactly one logical operation; no "and also" clauses
The creator always receives 70% of atomic credit; the rate cannot change without FORGE re-certification
PDDs scoring below 45/50 are returned for remediation
Compression keeps at least 97.5% semantic preservation; over-compression triggers the PRISM fallback
Tier gates are enforced server-side on req.localUser; client-side state is advisory only
All platform events are emitted to the telemetry streams (written as A–D); no domain may suppress telemetry
groConstraints are hard-coded as GRO SAFE\_LIFE; SAVANT never compresses GRO
A non-suppressible disclaimer on all F9 outputs, MAP economic projections and MDL Score outputs
The FORGE pipeline (written as F0–F9) is always available to the ARCHITECT tier without feature removal
The SPHINX obligation is complete at USDC credit; Single Value Parity is enforced globally
msdQuality is always sourced from F0.5 Native Engine session data
Every MDL Score output carries "Approximate Kolmogorov complexity — not exact." Non-suppressible
An interface contract (OpenAPI, DDL, Protobuf or TypeSpec) is produced before implementation code for any software artifact; code-first requests return to F1. Non-suppressible

No F0 source classification may be marketed as predictive without an attached empirical precision, recall or lead-time citation; outputs carry a confidence flag (EMPIRICALLY\_CALIBRATED, PROVISIONAL or THEORY\_ONLY). Non-suppressible
F5-Synth ranks marketplace SPCs by unbiased capability match only; sponsorship may reorder display, never the match itself
SAVANT verdicts are binary and evidence-based: FIT (≥ 88% fidelity) or CLUSTER (a governed Agentic Cluster); no partial-fit or degraded state may be reported
Every field in a platform-generated user artifact traces to explicit user entry or a verified platform record, with the source shown; no field is auto-filled with an unverified claim
All user-facing exports (first: Living Resume, D17)
A CELL produces exactly one MA per session: one task, one tool, one output
A CELL never produces an SPC; work that needs SPC architecture is handed to the FORGE pipeline
A CELL delivers a complete package: Classification Report, 3-document Micro PDD and Interface Contract
Never more than 3 Atomic Prompts per MA
Never a \[ROLE\] pillar in any MA Atomic Prompt
Never a DISC profile, Camelot Seat or personality on an MA
Never more than 1 primary tool interaction per MA
Escalate: a multi-tool agent is a task
Never production-ready if the ARES stress test fails
Hold until all 3 attack vectors pass
Never an MA for any function that violates GRO LOVE/HARM
Never guesses: every constraint finding comes from the MVE registry or a live scan
Never deploys a partial SPC: FIT (≥ 88%) or CLUSTER, nothing between
Never builds an ungoverned cluster: every MA inherits the source SPC's GRO constraints
No cluster with fewer than 3 MAs
No cluster with more than 12 MAs
Escalate to the FORGE SPC pipeline
No MA in a cluster carries a \[ROLE\] pillar
Every cluster has exactly one GRO Propagation Authority MA
A GRO Distribution Map is in every portability kit
Never alters the SPC's GRO Protocol during portability
Interface contracts use structured JSON schemas, never raw text
The IQS scoring algorithm is never compressed
The GRO ethics audit is never compressed
The FORGE certification structure is kept
Authentication and session security are kept
The upgrade path documentation is kept
The FORGE production ID format is kept
No user-facing feature may be CLASS C; if no CLASS B equivalent exists, change the platform, not the class
Infrastructure that serves only scale that does not yet exist is CLASS C
Every CLASS C deferral has a specific, measurable trigger
The MVP schema is forward-compatible: add fields, never rename or remove them
An MVP PDD that needs more than one person, or DevOps skills beyond a senior developer, is not compressed enough
User authentication flows are always CLASS A
The primary data store is always CLASS A
All user-visible UI components are always CLASS A
Error handling for user-facing operations is always CLASS A
Core business logic is always CLASS A
JCSE quality scoring in PDD outputs is always CLASS A
GRO state machine references are always CLASS A
ZPOS+5 optimisation of output content is always CLASS A
The FORGE Certification Block is always CLASS A
The Upgrade Path Document is always CLASS A
F9 is fail-closed: a build without the required evidence does not pass, and physical or firmware work needs external evidence before it moves on
ATLAS 360 SCAN of the ARK Harness (23 Sep 2026), as carried into the XVL PDD stage map
No stage handler waits for telemetry, and no telemetry failure reaches a user
A trace event never carries a prompt body, email or name; only identifiers and hashes
Consent is OFF until a scope says otherwise; a confidential artifact is never captured
No record is written without passing the consent check and the ethics gate in the same transaction
Every record states where its rejected output came from (observed, template or none)
Nothing estimated is presented as measured; unmeasured values are NULL or UNMEASURED
Governance events with no verified FM mapping stay UNMAPPED; no code is forced
FM-23 is assigned by the gate only
No dataset version is published without a dry run and a named human approval
Withdrawal produces a new version and discloses that earlier public versions cannot be recalled
No price, SKU, cash or tier logic in the Deck; virality never appears as value
Every GP(t) figure is labelled a design target pending Study C1
The Deck's self-claims of certification, scores and tiers are never repeated as facts
No stage grades its own work; self-attested results are recorded but never count as external evidence
Inconclusive is not a pass: errors, timeouts and missing evidence never produce PASS
Floors only go up: users add tracks above the F0 floor; only the named Principal lowers it, with a logged reason
No evidence, no verdict: a verdict without an evidence hash is rejected
Scores stay separate: track verdicts are never folded into one composite, and JCSE stays labelled self-assigned
No content leaves custody to an external track beyond the consent level its owner set
Labels are earned: Evidence-Backed needs a pass at I1 or higher; Independently Audited needs I3 by an outside auditor
Verify the premise first: no stage builds on a scientific or clinical claim whose integrity check is missing or Refuted (F0.5 onward)
AI judges do not certify science: Track J may comment on scientific validity but never passes it; that takes Track H
A Stream E triplet needs a FAIL and a later PASS on the same case, both at I1 or higher; self-attested results never make a triplet
Stream E rejected outputs are always OBSERVED; TEMPLATE is not allowed
Held-out cases are used only to measure; they never enter training data or exports
No self-modification: VTE proposes, a named person approves, nothing in the Harness changes automatically
Carries CD-03, CD-04, CD-08 and CD-09 into Stream E (consent OFF, one-transaction gate, FM-23 by the gate, no export without dry run and approval)
No improvement claims unless held-out results show it, labelled with the sample size
Required approvals are reported as governance touches, never as failed autonomy
Readiness levels are earned per pillar; one strong pillar never offsets a weak one
Readiness is a leading indicator only, always shown beside outcome metrics, never alone
An F12 incident is recorded as an I2 failure; no stage marks its own incident resolved
On a failed release check, roll back first; fix through the F-process
No self-hosted or air-gapped offering ships with an open SEC REP ONE critical finding
Carries XVL-01, CD-03, CD-09 and VTE-04
No product reaches F10 without a passing verification pack for its circuit
Only a named human answers the SC question; the Harness never answers Yes for the owner
Any product that runs on a physical device passes F9 MECHA, with external evidence, before F9.5 and F10
F9.5 and F10–F12 are never skipped; every route ends with custody, staged release, handoff and Operate
Every skipped stage is in the trace as SKIPPED\_BY\_SC; certificates name the circuit
A short-route product is never shown as having passed stages it skipped
The XVL profile floor set at F0 still applies; a circuit can add checks but never drop below it
Five tokens in fixed order (Title · Date-Time · Project · Author · Format) in every filename and in the document's metadata
A human is the author; no SPC, agent or model is named as author, and the AI team is disclosed inside
Clarity never changes meaning; protected spans are never edited
No document says built, certified, compliant or audited without evidence
SOCRATES flags but never edits; KLARITY edits but never approves; SKRIBE scores layout, not truth
KLARITY's three figures and SKRIBE's design score are never merged
Published means immutable; a re-publish is a new version
No Final document is released without a named approval
The curator is never listed as an author of cited research
No factual sentence ships without a Cited Works Ledger row
Unpublished, confidential and patent-pending work is described at outcome level only
Predictions, hypotheses, rankings and prize forecasts are labelled as opinion or inference
Humour never rests on a false premise and never targets authors, patients or groups
No creator is introduced to another without both accepting
No issue is released without a named human editor's approval
Clarity, Truthfulness and Detectability are never collapsed into one number

Run health checks each step against the previous version: errors, refusals, latency, cost and a Track E smoke evalset.
Roll back automatically on any failed check and open an F12 incident and a VTE failure case.
Sign a release record with version hashes, checks, decisions and approver.

Contain incidents by rollback or fail-closed and record the containment step.

Seed FM-XV-01 to FM-XV-12 in fm\_taxonomy with source\_status PROPOSED and empty patterns.
Define the signed xvl\_verdict event: trace\_id, stage, track, adapter, independence level, verdict, evidence hash, evalset case hash, split, artifact and version hash, model versions; no body.
Add stream E and the four VTE event types to the Command Deck trace contract and capture map; reject unknown values.
Write each verdict back to the trace spine as an event carrying stage, track, verdict and evidence hash only.
Emit one signed verdict event from XVL for every track run, through an outbox, without delaying the run.

Block self-hosted and air-gapped offerings until every SEC REP ONE critical control is closed.

Export an F5 SPC as AGENTS.md plus mirror files, and check the round trip.
Report disagreement between self-attested and external verdicts per stage.

Define the publishable\_source contract: source\_id, artifact\_type (MA, MICRO\_PDD, SPC, PDD, MVP\_PDD, LIVING\_PDD, F0\_SERVICE\_OUTPUT, SPC\_PLAYER\_OUTPUT), origin\_stage, version\_hash, project\_id, author\_ref, title, body\_ref, saved\_at. Reject any field outside the enums.
Define the Canonical Document Model (CDM) JSON schema: ordered blocks of heading, paragraph, list, table, callout, code, figure, worksheet\_row and metadata; each block carries a protected flag.
Accept a publish request only for a saved artifact with a version\_hash; snapshot that exact version so later edits never change a document in flight.
Build the F3 CELL Micro Agent adapter: map the five-section Birth Package and its Interface Contract into CDM blocks.
Build the F4 Micro PDD adapter: map the Cheat Sheet, Worksheet and Contract into CDM blocks.
Build the F5 SPC adapter: map the 15-section Super Prompt Card into CDM blocks, keeping the 7-pillar fields as tables.
Build the F6 ATLAS PDD adapter for both the 4-Part and the 12-Part (Parts 0–11) layouts; map worksheet rows to worksheet\_row blocks with their priority.
Build the F7 MVP PDD adapter: map the SPARTAN MVP-PDD and carry its public verification URL and certification ID as metadata, never as body text that KLARITY may edit.
Build the Living PDD adapter: publish a dated snapshot of the Living PDD at its current version hash and label the document 'Snapshot as of <date-time>'.
Build the F0 business-service adapter: map advisory, intake and diagnostic outputs into CDM blocks, tagging them as service output rather than certified artifacts.
Build the SPC Player adapter: map a saved SPC Player session output into CDM blocks with the playing SPC's name and version as metadata.
Define the naming rule: <Title>\_\_<Date-Time>\_\_<Project>\_\_<Author>\_\_<FORMAT>.<ext>, five tokens in this fixed order, joined by a double underscore.
Build the Title token from the artifact title: transliterate to ASCII, replace spaces and punctuation with hyphens, collapse repeats, cap at 60 characters. An empty title blocks publishing.
Build the Date-Time token at the moment rendering completes: YYYYMMDD-HHMM plus the time-zone abbreviation of the publisher's profile (default America/Chicago, e.g. 20261012-1434CDT).
Build the Project token from the ACC project record. A publish request with no project is blocked until the user picks one.
Build the Author token from the accountable human author (the signed-in publisher or the artifact's named Principal). Never use an SPC, an agent or a model name as the author.
Build the Format token (DOCX, PDF or HTML) and the matching lower-case extension; one filename per format.
Assemble the filename, enforce a 180-character limit by shortening only the Title token, and append -02, -03 on a same-minute collision.
Define the house design tokens: Navy #1B2A4A, Deep Navy #0D1B40, Gold #C9A227, Teal #1F6F6B; Cambria headings, Calibri body; margins, header and footer.
Build the title block: the five naming fields, production ID, status, Tier, JCSE line and confidentiality marking.
Write the same five fields into the document: the title block, DOCX core properties, PDF document info and HTML meta tags.
Offer four audience profiles (Executive, Technical, Client, Public), each with a target reading level, and store the choice on the publish job.
Mark protected spans before any edit: IDs, production IDs, numbers, scores, code, worksheet prompt text, quotes, legal text and verification URLs.
Run the plain-language pass on unprotected prose only, to the chosen reading level.
Build or extend the Definition of Terms from terms actually used in the document; keep an existing glossary's wording and add only missing terms.
Add a one-page summary only when the artifact has none, and label it 'Summary added by KLARITY'.
Extract every status claim (built, tested, certified, compliant, audited, production-ready) and every figure from the CDM.
Apply the Honesty Gate (G3): flag any status claim without an evidence tag, and any JCSE score not marked self-assigned.
Check internal consistency: counts against tables, scales against each other (for example a JST scale stated two ways), IDs and dates.
Never edit content. SOCRATES only flags and asks; edits come from the author or KLARITY.
Issue a verdict: CLEAR, CLEAR\_WITH\_NOTES or HOLD. HOLD blocks a Final publish until a named human resolves or overrides it with a written reason.
Report Clarity, Truthfulness and Detectability as three separate figures (KLARITY-003). A check that was not run shows 'not run', never zero and never an estimate.
Produce a change report: every edited sentence shown before and after, for the human reviewer.
Ask the author up to five dialectic questions on the weakest assumptions and attach them to the Publication Review Note.
Define one layout template per artifact type (eight templates), mapping CDM blocks to page styles.
Colour-code worksheet priorities in the MAX palette: P0 red, P1 amber, P2 blue, P3 grey.
Generate the table of contents and running header (title and production ID) and footer (page X of Y).
Switch wide worksheet tables to landscape sections (15840 × 12240 twips, 14400 DXA content width).
Print the disclosure footer on the last page: AI editorial team, human approver, Tier and 'AI-drafted; requires human review' when applicable.
Render DOCX from the CDM and the template with the Node.js docx library, following house rules: ShadingType.CLEAR fills, column widths summing to the content width, PageBreak inside a Paragraph.
Render PDF from the DOCX through LibreOffice headless so both formats share one layout; export tagged PDF.
Render HTML as one self-contained file with inline CSS, light and dark themes, phone-width layout and a print stylesheet.
Compute a content hash from the CDM text and record it on every format, so DOCX, PDF and HTML can be proven to carry the same content.
Validate each file: DOCX through validate.py, PDF pages rasterised with pdftoppm for a thumbnail check, HTML through a validator and link check.
Score the rendered layout on SKRIBE's five dimensions (/50). Below 38 blocks; 38–42 triggers one revision cycle; 43 or above may proceed. Shown separately from KLARITY's three figures.
Run the accessibility pass: heading order, alt text, text contrast of at least 4.5:1 and document language, targeting WCAG 2.2 AA.
Configure which stages show PUBLISH DOCUMENT: F0, F3, F4, F5, F6, F7, Living PDD view (F9.5), F10 and the SPC Player. Hidden at F1, F2, F8, F9 and F11 by default.
Enable the button only when the artifact is saved; otherwise show it disabled with the reason 'Save the artifact to publish it'.
Build the publish dialog: format checkboxes (DOCX, PDF, HTML), audience profile, Draft or Final, and a live preview of each filename.
Show job progress: QUEUED, NORMALISING, CLARIFYING, INTERROGATING, RENDERING, VALIDATING, AWAITING\_APPROVAL, then PUBLISHED, HELD or FAILED.
Build the review panel: page thumbnails, KLARITY change report, SOCRATES notes and verdict, SKRIBE design score and the three KLARITY figures.
Require a named human approval for a Final publish. Draft publishes skip approval but carry a DRAFT watermark on every page.
Add 'Approve and publish' for Final jobs, recording the approver's name and time.
Create the document\_library record: doc\_id, production ID, the five naming fields, source\_id and version\_hash, formats, content hash, scores, verdict and approver.
List publish history on each artifact: version, formats, date-time, approver and download links.
Inherit the source artifact's production ID when it has one; otherwise assign JNGL-DOC-<TYPE>-<YEAR>-<NNN>.
Store files encrypted at rest and private by default; sharing is an explicit action.
Serve downloads through signed links that expire.
Make every re-publish a new version linked to the one it supersedes; never overwrite a published file.
Hand published files to F10 export and F11 Host Connector destinations (for example Google Drive or SharePoint) when the connector is configured.
Emit a document\_published trace event to Command Deck MAX with the origin stage, identifiers and hashes only, never the body.
Write an audit event for each job state change: actor, action, time, source version hash and content hash.
Bind GRO states: LIFE by default; SAFE\_LIFE for legal, financial and health content (adds a not-advice notice and requires approval even for Draft); CONTAINMENT when a scan finds secrets.
Scan the CDM for secrets (API keys, tokens, connection strings) and personal data before rendering; secrets hold the job, personal data is flagged for the reviewer.
Default every document to 'Confidential — Internal'; changing the marking is an explicit, logged choice.
Enforce row-level security on document\_library by organisation and project.
Pass artifact text to the KLARITY and SOCRATES model calls as delimited data with no tool access, so instructions inside an artifact are never followed.
Golden set, Release 1: publish one saved SPC, ATLAS PDD and MVP PDD in DOCX, PDF and HTML and compare against reviewed reference files.
Golden set, Release 2: publish one saved MA, Micro PDD, Living PDD, F0 service output and SPC Player output in all three formats and compare against reviewed reference files.
Naming test: every produced filename matches the five-token pattern and its metadata matches its filename.
Parity test: DOCX, PDF and HTML of one job carry the same content hash.
Protected-span test: after the clarity pass, every ID, number, score, quote and code block is byte-identical to the source.
Seeded-claim test: an artifact containing 'FORGE Certified' with no evidence tag must receive HOLD.
Run a BUGMXT scan of the engine before each release; no open critical defect may ship.
